title: Design native PR landing behind a code-host interface
summary: Write docs/design/native-pr-landing.md designing how Athena pushes, opens, tracks and merges its own PRs per the 2026-10-12 addenda. All code-host operations sit behind a host-neutral interface, with GitHub as the first adapter only. Add a decisions.md entry; no code.

defaults_applied.how: Doc with alternatives, recommendation, open questions, review needs before any build.
Claims cite BRIEF.md and repo files with read/inferred labels.
Each rule names its enforcing mechanism or is marked prose-only.
One doc plus one decisions entry.
No secrets or personal data in the doc.

assumptions: Design only; no implementation, no trait code committed (the interface is specified in prose/signature sketches in the doc).
Credentials for the host adapter are handled by the host CLI/environment, never stored in files.
Review by a separate reviewer is requested after the doc, per the designed default, but review files are not part of this change.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/native-pr-landing.md exists with status, problem, alternatives (at least: Athena opens/merges PRs in core via a code-host interface; keep operator-driven PRs; hybrid), recommendation, and implementation plan; claims are marked read/inferred with file/line citations.

The design defines a code-host interface (a Rust trait: push branch, open PR, read status/checks, read comments, merge, close) with GitHub as the first adapter only. It lists the operations, a host-neutral vocabulary (change request rather than PR where practical), and what a second adapter (e.g. GitLab) would need. Nothing in core names GitHub types.
It cites the 2026-10-12 addenda in BRIEF.md ('Athena does what the operator should not have to'; 'Brownfield integration' stealth requirement) and states how each is met.

It covers the lifecycle: branch push, PR open, title/body from reading and verdict, CI wait, review comments as untrusted data, merge method including squash chains per docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md, and failure/rollback.
It states BRIEF.md constraints: only this repo, never push or open PRs upstream; third-party content untrusted; stealth mode adds no Athena files to PRs against third-party repos.
It names the mechanism enforcing each rule or marks it prose-only, and lists open questions and review needs.
docs/decisions.md gains one entry recording the design call, including the host-interface decision. No code, tests, or governance files change.
Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only the design doc (and optionally decisions.md/CHANGELOG.md) changed; no .rs, Cargo, athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflow files.

out_of_scope: Any implementation, Rust code, or tests
Adapters other than GitHub (only the interface is designed)
Changes to governance files, CI workflows, or athena.toml
Pushing or opening PRs against upstream or third-party repos
departures: Slightly lower cost and time than reference: docs-only change with no cold build beyond checks.
